key_insight: MonoArt progressively reasons about part structure to disentangle motion from geometry, enabling stable monocular estimation of articulation and 3D shape without heavy multi-view or retrieval supervision.
problem_solved: The paper addresses unstable and entangled articulation regression from a single image—where motion cues and object structure are mixed—while avoiding reliance on multi-view data, retrieval-based assembly, or expensive auxiliary supervision.
method: Progressive structural reasoning: predict a coarse part hierarchy/graph first, then refine parts and joint topology to provide a stable structural prior.
Articulation-aware parameter estimation: condition motion regression on the inferred structure to decouple motion and geometry and produce stable joint parameters.
Geometry refinement: iteratively refine part shapes and pose to produce an articulated 3D reconstruction from a single RGB image with improved accuracy and efficiency.
impact: Provides a scalable, efficient route to recover articulated 3D models from single images, lowering supervision and compute barriers for applications in robotics, AR/VR, and animation. Practitioners can integrate structure-first reasoning to improve robustness of single-view 3D pipelines.

paper_title: MonoArt: Progressive Structural Reasoning for Monocular Articulated 3D Reconstruction
paper_authors: Haitian Li, Haozhe Xie, Junxiang Xu, Beichen Wen, Fangzhou Hong
